sentences.latin: Vir et uxor agrum parvum habent.
sentences.english: The man and the wife have a small field.

sentences.latin: Vir equum bonum ducit.
sentences.english: The man leads a good horse.

sentences.latin: Uxor aquam ad mensam portat.
sentences.english: The wife carries water to the table.

sentences.latin: Vir agrum suum amat.
sentences.english: The man loves his own field.

sentences.latin: Uxor cibum bonum parat.
sentences.english: The wife prepares good food.

sentences.latin: Vir piscem in flumine capit.
sentences.english: The man catches a fish in the river.

sentences.latin: Uxor virum suum vocat.
sentences.english: The wife calls her own husband.

sentences.latin: Vir piscem uxori dat.
sentences.english: The man gives the fish to the wife.

sentences.latin: Uxor piscem parvum laudat.
sentences.english: The wife praises the small fish.

sentences.latin: Vir florem pulchrum videt.
sentences.english: The man sees a beautiful flower.

sentences.latin: Vir uxori florem dat.
sentences.english: The man gives the flower to the wife.

sentences.latin: Uxor florem novum amat.
sentences.english: The wife loves the new flower.

sentences.latin: Vir donum novum emit.
sentences.english: The man buys a new gift.

sentences.latin: Uxor donum novum capit.
sentences.english: The wife takes the new gift.

sentences.latin: Uxor donum novum aperit.
sentences.english: The wife opens the new gift.

sentences.latin: Uxor virum bonum laudat.
sentences.english: The wife praises the good husband.

sentences.latin: Vir et uxor mensam parant.
sentences.english: The man and the wife prepare the table.

sentences.latin: Vir avem in arbore videt.
sentences.english: The man sees a bird in the tree.

sentences.latin: Uxor avem pulchram audit.
sentences.english: The wife hears the beautiful bird.

sentences.latin: Vir et uxor cibum bonum habent.
sentences.english: The man and the wife have good food.

sentences.latin: Vir et uxor templum magni dei petunt.
sentences.english: The man and the wife make for the temple of the great god.

sentences.latin: Uxor deo donum pulchrum in templo dat.
sentences.english: In the temple, the wife gives a beautiful gift to the god.

sentences.latin: Vir deum sapientem magna voce laudat.
sentences.english: The man praises the wise god with a loud voice.

sentences.latin: Nox nigra virum et uxorem terret.
sentences.english: The black night frightens the man and the wife.

sentences.latin: Draco magnus et ferox oppidum petit.
sentences.english: A great and fierce dragon attacks the town.

sentences.latin: Vir uxorem suam de periculo monet.
sentences.english: The man warns his own wife about the danger.

sentences.latin: Itaque uxor viro suo fideli credit.
sentences.english: And so the wife trusts her own faithful husband.

sentences.latin: Canis niger et fidelis portam magnam custodit.
sentences.english: The black and faithful dog guards the great gate.

sentences.latin: Vir canem fortem et fidelem laudat.
sentences.english: The man praises the brave and faithful dog.

sentences.latin: Itaque deus virum et uxorem servat.
sentences.english: And so the god protects the man and the wife.

sentences.latin: Donum novum deo a viro et uxore datur.
sentences.english: A new gift is given to the god by the man and the wife.

sentences.latin: Uxor cibum multum suae familiae parat.
sentences.english: The wife prepares much food for her own family.

sentences.latin: Vir uxori in via verba dulcia dicit.
sentences.english: On the road, the man says sweet words to the wife.

sentences.latin: Nam uxor virum suum fidelem amat.
sentences.english: For the wife loves her own faithful husband.

sentences.latin: Itaque uxor viro suo felix respondet.
sentences.english: And so the happy wife answers her own husband.

sentences.latin: Verba dulcia in via a viro dicuntur.
sentences.english: Sweet words are said on the road by the man.

sentences.latin: Itaque pax oppido a deo servatur.
sentences.english: And so peace is preserved for the town by the god.

sentences.latin: Vir et uxor deum iustum laudant.
sentences.english: The man and the wife praise the just god.

sentences.latin: Vir et uxor multos amicos habent.
sentences.english: The man and the wife have many friends.

sentences.latin: Itaque vir et uxor felices viam longam petunt.
sentences.english: And so the happy man and wife make for the long road.

sentences.latin: Vir vetus et uxor fidelis vitam longam et difficilem habent.
sentences.english: The old man and the faithful wife have a long and difficult life.

sentences.latin: Fama praeclara viri sapientis et uxoris eius per civitatem scitur.
sentences.english: The brilliant fame of the wise man and of his wife is known throughout the community.

sentences.latin: Sed vir vetus et uxor fidelis gravi periculo maris terrentur.
sentences.english: But the old man and the faithful wife are frightened by the grave danger of the sea.

sentences.latin: Itaque uxor sapiens deum immortalem pro viro suo vocat.
sentences.english: And so the wise wife calls upon the immortal god on behalf of her own husband.

sentences.latin: Vir a gravi periculo ab uxore sua fideli et forti servatur.
sentences.english: The husband is saved from the grave danger by his faithful and brave wife.

sentences.latin: Virtus magna et vera uxoris sapientis a viro laudatur.
sentences.english: The great and true courage of the wise wife is praised by the husband.

sentences.latin: Nam fatum grave vitam viri et uxoris regit.
sentences.english: For grave fate rules the life of the man and of the wife.

sentences.latin: Sed veritas clara eorum ab omni populo scitur.
sentences.english: But their clear truth is known by all the people.

sentences.latin: Itaque nomen praeclarum viri et uxoris in aeternitate servatur.
sentences.english: And so the illustrious name of the man and of the wife is preserved in eternity.

sentences.latin: Nam vir et uxor vitam veram et bonam habent.
sentences.english: For the man and the wife have a true and good life.
